text: **dsh-rustxng**（DSH 网页插件）：将自托管 RustXNG 接入 DSH 搜索。通过 Web provider 替换 web_search，提供 rustxng_search 和 rustxng_status 工具，以及 Plugins 设置卡片。还支持按需启动实例和可选的网页字符集修复。适合希望使用自有搜索服务或处理 meta 标签编码网页的用户。需 Node.js 20+、兼容版 DSH 和 RustXNG；默认可按需下载并启动服务。

**dsh-rustxng** connects DSH web_search to a self-hosted RustXNG server. It adds engine and category filters, status tools, a Plugins settings card, on-demand server startup, and optional charset repair for fetched pages. Requires Node.js 20+, compatible DSH, and RustXNG.

**dsh-rustxng** 的功能「替换网页搜索」：将 rustxng provider 注册到 DSH Web seam，并可选择为 web_search 提供结果。启用并选中后，搜索请求转发到配置的 RustXNG 实例。
**dsh-rustxng** 的功能「筛选式搜索工具」：agent 可调用 rustxng_search 并传入查询、结果数、引擎、类别、语言和时间范围，工具将 RustXNG 返回的来源整理成文本结果。
**dsh-rustxng** 的功能「实例状态查询」：调用 rustxng_status 查看本地服务是否可达、版本和已启用引擎数量，并读取 provider 选择和插件配置状态；该查询不会启动实例。
**dsh-rustxng** 的功能「字符集修复抓取」：启用 webFetch 后注册 rustxng-http provider，按 BOM、HTTP 头和 meta 标签识别编码，再用 TextDecoder 解码页面。
**dsh-rustxng** 的功能「按需管理 RustXNG」：搜索时发现服务不可达且 autoStart 开启，插件查找或下载匹配平台的二进制并启动，等待健康检查成功；其启动的进程可在空闲超时后停止。
**dsh-rustxng** 使用前须知：搜索会发送到配置的 RustXNG HTTP 地址，默认是本机 127.0.0.1:8888；实例需可访问，bundle 可配置为在首次搜索时下载并启动它。

[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) — and answer the
built-in **`web_search`** with it.

dsh-rustxng README · dsh-rustxng：RustXNG is a SearXNG-compatible metasearch engine written in Rust: one query fans out to
over a hundred search engines (119 enabled in 0.28's default `standard` profile),
deduplicates the results and returns them without ads or tracking. This
plugin connects DSH to a RustXNG you run yourself (Windows, macOS or Linux)
and adds:

dsh-rustxng README · dsh-rustxng：| Contribution | What it gives you |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Search provider** | A `rustxng` provider on the web seam. Point `web.searchProvider` at it and the built-in `web_search` is answered by your instance — no DeepSeek search API key involved. |
| **Settings card** | A card in **Plugins** with two live switches and the instance URL. No restart, no hand-edited YAML. |
| **Tools** | `rustxng_search` (engine, category, language and time-range scoped) and `rustxng_status` (reachability, version, engine count, provider state). |
| **Fetch provider** (optional) | A charset-aware `web_fetch`: resolves BOM → HTTP header → `<meta charset>` before decoding, so Shift_JIS pages that declare their encoding only in `<meta>` stop coming back as `�`. Does not use RustXNG. |
| **Process supervision** (optional) | Start the binary when the instance does not answer, and stop it again after an idle timeout (default 60 min, editable in the card). Only a process this plugin started is stopped — this is also the only thing that cleans up after a Harness that was killed. |
| **Binary fetcher** | `node scripts/install-binary.mjs` downloads and verifies the right release b

dsh-rustxng README · dsh-rustxng：Nothing in DSH is patched: the plugin uses the documented `ctx.web.registerSearchProvider()`
API and the ordinary `web.searchProvider` settings field, so it survives Harness upgrades.

dsh-rustxng README · Do you need this plugin at all?：**If you use rustdsh (`rdsh`), let rustdsh handle search.** Since v0.15.0 it checks whether
rustxng / `SEARXNG_URL` actually answers at start-up and, only when it does, passes
`DSH_WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDER=rdsh-rustxng` to the delegated DSH so the bundled
`rdsh-web-search-searxng` provider takes `web_search` over (`web_search_bridge`, on by
default).
section: Do you need this plugin at all?

text:
dsh-rustxng README · Do you need this plugin at all?：| Your situation | Use |
| :--- | :--- |
| You start **DSH through rdsh** (`rdsh tui`, `rdsh web`, …) and want `web_search` to hit a local engine | **rustdsh's own bridge.** Nothing to configure; stop it with `rdsh features off web_search_bridge` |
| You start **`dsh` directly** (desktop app, systemd, …) and want `web_search` replaced | **This plugin.** rdsh only injects into the children it launches, so a plain `dsh` boot is untouched |
| You need **`web_fetch` to stop garbling** pages whose charset is declared only in `<meta>` | **This plugin** (`webFetch.enabled`) — rustdsh's bridge is search only |
| You want the agent to call RustXNG **as a tool** (`rustxng_search` / `rustxng_status`) | **This plugin.** |
| You want the binary **downloaded, started and idle-stopped** for you | **This plugin** (`autoStart`); rustdsh never downloads anything on behalf of the bridge |
| You use both and want **one instance for both** | Point rdsh at this plugin's instance: `RUSTXNG_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8888` |
section: Do you need this plugin at all?

text:
dsh-rustxng README · Do you need this plugin at all?：**Give search to exactly one of them.** With both, two providers are registered (`rustxng` and
`rdsh-rustxng`) and two sidecars can end up running. Letting rustdsh own it means turning this
plugin's `webSearch.enabled` off; letting this plugin own it means
`rdsh features off web_search_bridge` (or `RDSH_WEB_SEARCH_BRIDGE=0`).

dsh-rustxng README · Requirements：- DeepSeek Harness `>= 0.2.0-rc.2 < 0.3.0` (host `tools`, `web` and `settings` services).
  Verified on **0.2.0-rc.2** and **0.2.1-rc.2**; see [docs/PLATFORMS.md](docs/PLATFORMS.md#dsh-versions).

dsh-rustxng README · 1. Get RustXNG：**Easiest:** let the plugin fetch a release binary.

```bash
node scripts/install-binary.mjs          # into $DSH_HOME/bin (or ~/.dsh/bin)
node scripts/install-binary.mjs --dir ./bin --musl   # Linux without glibc
```

The script picks the asset for your platform, verifies the published SHA-256, and prints
the start command.

**Or** download it yourself from the
[releases page](https://github.com/sahenjp/RustXNG/releases/latest):

dsh-rustxng README · 1. Get RustXNG：| Platform | Asset |
| :--- | :--- |
| Windows x64 | `rustxng-v<ver>-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe` |
| macOS arm64 | `rustxng-v<ver>-aarch64-apple-darwin` |
| macOS x64 | `rustxng-v<ver>-x86_64-apple-darwin` |
| Linux x64 (glibc) | `rustxng-v<ver>-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` |
| Linux x64 (musl) | `rustxng-v<ver>-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` |

Start it:

```bash
rustxng --port 8888                       # listens on 127.0.0.1:8888 by default
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8888/healthz'      # → OK
```

Installing from a checkout **links** the directory, so Node resolves the plugin's real path

text:
dsh-rustxng README · 3. Turn it on：Open **Plugins → RustXNG** and switch on *Use RustXNG for web_search*. Or set it in your
profile patch (`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- id: dsh-rustxng
  config:
    baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:8888
    webSearch:

From then on `web_search` is answered by RustXNG. The `enabled` and `autoSelect` switches
and the instance URL are *volatile*: the settings card changes them live, and turning the
feature off hands `web.searchProvider` back to whatever it was before.

dsh-rustxng README · Configuration：| Key | Default | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch; `false` unloads the tools and unregisters the provider. |
| `baseUrl` | `http://127.0.0.1:8888` | Where RustXNG listens. Volatile (editable in the card). |
| `timeoutMs` | `20000` | Timeout for one search. |
| `defaultLimit` | `12` | Sources handed to `web_search` (1–50). |
| `language` | `''` | Search language (`ja`, `en`, …); empty = instance default. |
| `timeRange` | `''` | `day` / `week` / `month` / `year`; empty = no filter. |
| `safeSearch` | `-1` | `-1` = instance default, else `0` / `1` / `2`. |
| `categories` | `[]` | Category filters applied to every search (`general`, `it`, …). |
| `exposeTools` | `true` | Register `rustxng_search` / `rustxng_status`. |
| `webSearch.enabled` | `false` | Replace the built-in `web_search`. Volatile. |
| `webSearch.autoSelect` | `true` | Write `web.searchProvider = 'rustxng'` for you. Volatile. |
| `webFetch.enabled` | `false` | Replace `web_fetch` with the charset-aware fetcher. Volatile. |
| `webFetch.autoSelect` | `true` | Write `web.fetchProvider = 'rustxng-http'` for you. Volatile. |
| `autoStart.enabled` | `true

dsh-rustxng README · Optional: charset-aware fetch：The built-in HTTP fetcher reads `charset` from the `Content-Type` header only. Many Japanese
sites (JRA, municipal sites, older corporate sites) send `text/html` with the encoding
declared *only* in `<meta charset="Shift_JIS">`, so the page arrives as replacement
characters. Turning on `webFetch.enabled` registers a small provider that resolves
**BOM → HTTP header → `<meta>`** and decodes with `TextDecoder` (Node ships the legacy
encodings), with a size cap and the same html/text classification.

dsh-rustxng README · Optional: charset-aware fetch：```yaml
- id: dsh-rustxng
  config:
    webFetch:
      enabled: true

It does not touch RustXNG: it is plain HTTP plus decoding. Leave it off if you prefer the
built-in fetcher.

dsh-rustxng README · Optional: charset-aware fetch：> **On hosts that hide the `web` settings row** (DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 publishes only entries with a
> volatile field), `autoSelect` cannot write the selection — it needs the same context rules
> as the search side. Set both fields in the profile patch, exactly as above; the card's
> switches then still control whether the plugin is active. `rustxng_status` says so:
> `Fetch provider: enabled, but the selection was not written (…)`.

dsh-rustxng README · First run: nothing is installed yet：The plugin does not bundle the binary and ships with the replacement **off**, so a fresh
install answers like this until one of the two paths below is taken:

```
RustXNG could not be reached: fetch failed (connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:8888)
Start it (for example `rustxng --port 8888`), or point the `baseUrl` setting at your instance.
```

text:
dsh-rustxng README · First run: nothing is installed yet：**Easiest:** the shipped bundle already has *Start RustXNG automatically* on, so the first search fetches and starts the instance; nothing to click. On the next start it
downloads the matching release (SHA-256 verified, ~22-27 MB) into `$DSH_HOME/bin`, starts it,
and stops it again after the idle timeout. Nothing else to install.

**Manual:** `npx dsh-rustxng-fetch` drops the binary in the same place; run it yourself, or
wire it into launchd / systemd and leave auto-start off.

dsh-rustxng README · First run: nothing is installed yet：The download never depends on GitHub's API: if the "latest release" lookup is rate-limited it
falls back to a pinned version, and `autoStart.binaryPath` (or `--version`) needs no lookup at
all.

text:
dsh-rustxng README · About the automatic selection：`autoSelect` writes `web.searchProvider = 'rustxng'` for you, but a plugin cannot do that
while it is mounting: the loader runs `apply()` inside its own transaction and rejects the
settings write with *"HMR transactions cannot be nested"*. 0.3.0 therefore retries the write
from a context that is allowed to write — a tool call (`rustxng_status` / `rustxng_search`) or
a live settings change from the card — and reports the outcome in `rustxng_status`.

dsh-rustxng README · About the automatic selection：If it still cannot be written (for example on a host that refuses plugin-initiated writes),
set the field once by hand; it is remembered:

```yaml
- id: web
  config:
    searchProvider: rustxng
    fetchProvider: http

dsh-rustxng README · Optional: start and stop the instance：If you would rather not run RustXNG as a service, let the plugin own the process:

```yaml
- id: dsh-rustxng
  config:
    autoStart:
      enabled: true

section: Optional: start and stop the instance

text:
dsh-rustxng README · Optional: start and stop the instance：- It starts the binary only when the instance does not already answer, and waits for
  `/healthz` before using it. Concurrent callers share one attempt, so two starts cannot race
  for the port.
- It **stops only a process it started** — a systemd unit or a manually started instance is
  never touched.
- On plugin unload (a normal DSH shutdown) it stops the process immediately.
- A Harness that is killed never runs that cleanup, so the **idle timeout** finishes the job:
  after `idleMinutes` without a search the process is stopped, and the next search starts it
  again. Reachability probes do not count as activity.
- `rustxng_status` reports `Auto-start: on — managed (pid …), idle timeout 60 min (12 min idle)`
  and `Selection: web.searchProvider: rustxng (this plugin), web.fetchProvider: http`.
- The `rustxng_search` tool starts the instance too, so a tool-only setup (no replacement of
  `web_search`) also works from the first call. `rustxng_status` never starts it — it only
  reports.
- **Which version is downloaded:** always the latest release. The tag is resolved through
  GitHub's release API and, when that is rate-lim

text:
dsh-rustxng README · If you also use rdsh：- **`rdsh search-web --engine rustxng`** — a shell command for rdsh's own search
  (`SEARXNG_URL` → `RUSTXNG_URL` → a local `rustxng` → `127.0.0.1:8888`);
  `rdsh rustxng install` puts the binary in `~/.local/bin`.
- **`web_search_bridge`** (v0.15.0+, on by default) — injects
  `DSH_WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDER=rdsh-rustxng` into a DSH that rdsh launches, so the bundled
  `rdsh-web-search-searxng` provider serves `web_search`. A plain `dsh` boot sees none of it.

dsh-rustxng README · If you also use rdsh：So search is already handled in a rustdsh-driven session: leave this plugin's
`webSearch.enabled` off there. Turn it on — and stop the bridge with
`rdsh features off web_search_bridge` — when you want the Harness-side replacement from a
direct `dsh` start, the model-facing tools, or managed download/start/idle-stop.

`web_fetch` is outside the bridge either way. If you run both, one instance can serve both:

dsh-rustxng README · If you also use rdsh：- point rdsh at the plugin's instance with `RUSTXNG_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8888`, or
- let the plugin reuse rdsh's binary: the search order is `autoStart.binaryPath` →
  `$DSH_HOME/bin` → `~/.local/bin` → `PATH`, and `rustxng_status` prints which file is
  actually running (`Auto-start: on — managed (pid …) [rustxng]`).

Set `autoStart.binaryPath` when you have several builds and want a specific one.

dsh-rustxng README · Platform support：See [docs/PLATFORMS.md](docs/PLATFORMS.md) for how each platform is expected to be
verified, binary placement, and the platform-specific notes (PATH, service managers, WSL,

dsh-rustxng README · Upstream versions：This plugin talks only to RustXNG's SearXNG-compatible surface (`/healthz`, `/search?format=json`,
`/config`, `--bind`/`--port`/`RUSTXNG_IDLE_TIMEOUT`) and does not check a version, so a new
upstream release is normally a no-op here. The rules for when it is not — the two verification
tiers, what `PINNED_VERSION` means, and the five upstream changes that trigger a smoke run — are
in [docs/UPSTREAM.md](docs/UPSTREAM.md), together with a log of the changes already handled
(the default port moving to 29483, and the Google engine removals).

dsh-rustxng README · Troubleshooting：| Symptom | Fix |
| :--- | :--- |
| `RustXNG is not answering at …` | Start the instance, or fix `baseUrl` in the card. `rustxng_status` shows the probe error. |
| `web_search` still fails with a DeepSeek 401 | The provider is not selected: check the card's first switch, or `web.searchProvider` on the official *Web search* page. On DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 that field is not writable from a plugin — set it in the profile patch (see above) or with `DSH_WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDER=rustxng`. |
| Card missing from Plugins | The plugin row is not active — check Plugin Manager, and that the DSH version matches `dsh.compatibility`. On a linked checkout the schema comes through the Harness installation: `rustxng_status` prints `Config schema: loaded via …` or the resolution error. 0.1.2 resolves symlinked launchers such as `<prefix>/bin/dsh`. |
| `rustxng_status` says `Replace web_search: no (default)` although it is on | Fixed in 0.1.2 (live config values were compared as primitives). |
| `Wanted to register a provider but web is missing` | The profile has no `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web`; this plugin needs it for the replacement (the tools still work). |
| Results look thin |

RustXNG itself is **AGPL-3.0-or-later** and is *not* bundled here: the plugin talks to a
